record.paper_title: 20 Open Questions About Deformations of Compactifiable Manifolds
record.original_question: For the noncompact threefolds W_k = Tot(O_P1(-k) ⊕ O_P1(k - 2)), describe all deformations that are projectivizable.

evidence.quote: Question 9. Describe all projectivizable deformations of Wk.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For each integer $k$, let $W_k$ denote the noncompact complex threefold given by the total space of the rank-two holomorphic vector bundle
$$W_k \;=\; \operatorname{Tot}\!\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(k-2)\bigr)\longrightarrow \mathbb{P}^1.$$
A deformation of $W_k$ is a proper flat family $\mathcal{W}\to\Delta$ over a disk (or, more generally, a flat family of complex manifolds) whose central fiber is $W_k$. Such a deformation is called projectivizable if there exists a relative compactification of $\mathcal{W}\to\Delta$ to a flat family $\overline{\mathcal{W}}\to\Delta$ whose fibers are smooth projective threefolds containing the corresponding fibers of $\mathcal{W}$ as Zariski open subsets.

Problem. Describe (classify) all projectivizable deformations of $W_k$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem appears as one of a list of explicitly open questions about deformations of compactifiable manifolds. A targeted web search did not surface any subsequent work providing a complete classification of projectivizable deformations of the threefolds $W_k=\operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(-k)\oplus\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb{P}^1}(k-2))$, so the question appears to remain open.
